guarantees.claim: On negedge rst_ni, sp_enc_err_q is asynchronously cleared to 0. On posedge clk_i when rst_ni is high, if sp_enc_err_d is high, sp_enc_err_q is set to 1; otherwise sp_enc_err_q retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: sp_enc_err_d must be a synchronous signal stable at posedge clk_i, meeting setup/hold constraints.
assumptions.risk: If sp_enc_err_d is asynchronous or glitchy, the error could be missed or capture a metastable value, causing sp_enc_err_q to be incorrectly low or high.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni de-assertion must meet recovery/removal timing relative to clk_i to avoid metastability in sp_enc_err_q.
assumptions.risk: sp_enc_err_q may enter a metastable state or be set unexpectedly during reset de-assertion.

uncertain_points.claim: sp_enc_err_q is a sticky error flag that can only be cleared by a full reset. It is unclear if this sticky-only behavior is intentional per the design specification, or if a software-writable clear mechanism is missing.
uncertain_points.cond: when sp_enc_err_q is set and must be cleared for continued operation
uncertain_points.risk: If a software-clearable error is expected, lack of clear can lead to unrecoverable error state, potentially causing denial of service or blocking further operations until power-on reset.
